Key points
• Vitamin K is a term that includes phylloquinone and 10 menaquinone forms.
• Whereas phylloquinone is well characterized in the food supply, menaquinones have not been systematically analyzed,
which limits their use in dietary assessment.
• Phylloquinone absorption is lipid-driven whereas less is known about absorption of menaquinones.
• All vitamin K forms serve as an enzyme cofactor and support gamma-carboxylation of vitamin K-dependent coagulation
proteins. Multiple vitamin K-dependent extra-hepatic proteins exist but less is known about their role in human health.
• Non-enzymatic roles for vitamin K are emerging but the research is still in its infancy.
